subject: Observability forwarding & gateway options for Helios private deployment
messages:
From: Juan Perez <juan.perez@heliosbank.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: DevOps Team <devops@heliosbank.com>, Security Ops <security_ops@heliosbank.com>
Date: 2028-05-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Observability for private deploy — initial questions

Neha — thanks again for the run-through yesterday. We want to lock down how Helios will receive observability signals from Redwood's private (VPC) deployment. A few important constraints from our side:

- No internet-facing collectors are allowed — all egress must be via approved egress points (NAT or PrivateLink).
- Mutual TLS for any push connections; certs must be rotated and audit-able.
- We want traces (OTLP), metrics (Prometheus remote_write preferred), and logs (either HEC/Syslog or S3 export) to end up in our Splunk cluster.
- Minimal burst/peaky egress without buffering causing data loss — we need backpressure behavior documented.

Can you outline the recommended architectures and the authN/authZ options (client certs vs token-based vs VPC endpoint identities)? Also any firewall rules / ports we need to open and where Redwood vs Helios owns what.

Thanks — happy to set a call if it's easier.

—Juan
Juan Perez
Senior InfoSec Engineer | Helios Bank
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Juan Perez <juan.perez@heliosbank.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-05-30T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Observability for private deploy — initial questions

Juan — appreciate the constraints, very helpful. Below are three pragmatic patterns (tradeoffs called out) that customers commonly pick for private deployments. I've attached a draft gateway diagram and an authN/AuthZ options note.

1) Push-forwarder (preferred when low-latency traces/logs required)
   - Agent (Vector/Fluent Bit) running in customer VPC (sidecar or central forwarder) pushes to a Helios-managed collector endpoint (Splunk HEC or our forwarding gateway) over mTLS.
   - Auth: client certs issued by Redwood CA (we can do CA cross-signing with Helios) OR Helios-issued client certs accepted by the gateway. Rotation via short-lived certs + ACME-like renewal.
   - Network: allow outbound 443/tcp to a narrow set of collector IPs or PrivateLink endpoint. Use TLS SNI and client cert for mutual auth.
   - Pros: low latency, immediate traces/alerts.
   - Cons: requires limited egress; cert management responsibility needs to be agreed.

2) Pull-ish via S3/Storage staging (good when strict egress rules disallow direct collector connectivity)
   - Forwarder uploads compressed batches to an S3 bucket (or equivalent) in Helios account via VPC endpoint (no internet egress). Helios picks up and ingests into Splunk.
   - Auth: IAM role / STS with scoped credentials, or pre-signed URLs for ingestion.
   - Pros: no direct outbound to Splunk; easier firewall rules.
   - Cons: higher latency; need idempotency and ordering; storage retention must be defined.

3) Broker via message queue (Kafka/SQS) inside Helios VPC
   - Forwarder publishes to a queue over PrivateLink or VPC peering. Helios consumers read, transform, and send to Splunk.
   - Auth: mTLS + IAM or Kerberos depending on queue.
   - Pros: buffering/backpressure handled by queue; resilient to spikes.
   - Cons: extra component operationally; network connectivity still required.

Metrics and tracing specifics:
- Metrics: we recommend Prometheus remote_write from a push gateway (or scrape -> remote_write) to your remote_write endpoint over TLS. remote_write supports batching and should be rate-limited by the agent.
- Tracing: OTLP over gRPC with mTLS. Keep spans small; we can instrument Redwood runtime to reduce KV-cache leak (we'll document sensitive fields).

Firewall/Network rules (high level):
- Allow outbound TCP 443 to: <collector-ip-range> or PrivateLink endpoint ENI — we will provide the CIDRs once you choose an option.
- DNS: allow resolve for the gateway hostname; we recommend CNAME to the PrivateLink endpoint.
- For S3: allow putObject to the named bucket and STS:AssumeRole if using cross-account roles.

AuthN/AuthZ options (tradeoffs):
- mTLS (client cert): Strong auth, non-repudiation; requires cert issuance + rotation.
- Short-lived tokens (STS/OAuth): easier rotation, central revocation, but token leak window needs mitigation.
- Identity-based (PrivateLink + VPC endpoint policy + IAM): very restricted network-level control, minimal credentials to manage.

Next steps I propose:
- Confirm which pattern Helios prefers (1/2/3).
- Share any strict port/IP requirements so we can map the correct PrivateLink/NAT design.
- We'll produce a hardened runbook (ingest SLAs, retry/backoff, example agent config, and cert rotation steps).

I'll coordinate with Karthik for the low-level runbook and with Marissa/Naomi for compliance evidence (retention, audit logs). If helpful, we can do a 30-min tech deep-dive tomorrow.

Cheers,
Neha Kapoor

Quick technical notes from the runtime/infra side:

- For push-forwarder (option 1): ensure the agent implements retry with exponential backoff and bounded local buffering (disk-backed) to avoid OOM during spikes. We'll supply recommended Vector config snippets.
- Tracing: Redwood runtime will redact user PII from trace attributes by default, but we need Helios to confirm any PCI/PII fields to keep out of spans. We'll add a required config knob for additional filters.
- KV cache & metrics: some internal metrics expose model cache hit/miss rates; those should be tagged and can be redacted.
- Network specifics: if using PrivateLink we can publish a VPC endpoint service; Helios will create the endpoint in their account and attach endpoint policy. That avoids NAT egress.
- Audit logs: we can emit a signed ingestion receipt for each batch (digest + timestamp) to provide an immutable ingestion trail if required by compliance.

I'll draft the Vector/Fluent Bit snippets and an mtls cert rotation playbook (how to rotate with zero drop). Will drop those into the Drive link Neha shared.

—Karthik
